title: Slow memory leak
story: Every request adds 400 KiB to a cache that is never evicted. More memory only buys time. Expected: a stopgap or an escalation, and the diagnosis names the leak.

timeline.thought:
## Diagnosis

**Root cause: unbounded memory growth in the catalog process, not a one-off memory spike.**

Evidence:
- OOM kill log: `memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process 29297 (rss 129 MiB > limit 128 MiB)` — container hit its 128 MiB limit (`mem_limit_mb: 128.0`, `mem_peak_mb: 125.1`).
- The "response cache" grew from **39 MiB → 78 MiB in ~4 seconds** (`100 entries, 39 MiB` at 21:53:15 → `200 entries, 78 MiB` at 21:53:19), i.e. roughly **~10 MiB/s** growth, with CPU basically idle the whole time (`cpu_pct_avg_total: 0.9%`, `cpu_pct_peak_total: 3.0%`). This is not a load-driven cache that stabilizes — it's a linear, unbounded climb.
- Post-restart confirmation via `get_status`: only **12.5 seconds** after the restart the container is already back at **126.1 MiB / 128 MiB** — i.e. it is about to OOM again almost immediately, which rules out "transient traffic spike" and confirms a continuous leak.
- The compose file also wires in an env var `LEAK_KB` (`environment: - LEAK_KB=${CATALOG_LEAK_KB}`), consistent with a deliberate/uncapped memory-leak behavior in the app rather than normal cache sizing.

Given the ~10 MiB/s growth rate, even the maximum allowed memory (512m, guardrail `max_memory`) would only buy roughly (512-128)/10 ≈ 38 extra seconds before the next OOM — it would not resolve the incident, only delay the next crash loop. Per policy, a resource change should not be applied when it won't fix the actual cause (an unbounded/leaking cache, likely a code or config bug tied to `CATALOG_LEAK_KB`/cache eviction logic). This is outside what `set_memory` can remedy.

I will not apply a memory bump that is known to be insufficient against an unbounded leak, and `allowed_actions` only permits `set_memory` (no cpus/replica change applicable here anyway since it's stateless-singleton bound by `max_replicas: 1`). This needs code/config remediation (cache eviction/cap, or disabling/fixing the leak simulation), which is beyond guardrail resource tuning.

args.reason: catalog's in-process response cache shows unbounded growth (39 MiB→78 MiB in ~4s, ~10 MiB/s) causing OOM kill at 128 MiB limit (rss 129 MiB > limit 128 MiB, exit 137). Post-restart it already reached 126.1/128 MiB again within 12.5s, confirming a continuous leak rather than a sizing issue. Compose wires in an env var CATALOG_LEAK_KB, consistent with an uncapped leak/missing cache eviction in app code. Raising memory to the guardrail max (512m) would only delay the next OOM by seconds to tens of seconds, not resolve it, so no resource change inside the guardrails fixes the root cause. Needs a code/config fix (cache eviction policy or disabling the leak condition) and review of CATALOG_LEAK_KB/CATALOG_MODE settings.
